#1303. Fabregas: ‘Como came close to Inter victory before, Arteta inspirational’

Cesc Fabregas feels Como are facing ‘the strongest team in Italy’ and can get a result against Inter, having ‘come close three times,’ while Arsenal’s Mikel Arteta was impressed by the 9-1 victory at Lens.

It kicks off at San Siro on Sunday at 17.00 GMT (18.00 CET).

This is no longer just a battle for the top four, but a true Scudetto showdown, as Como have gone from strength to strength even with the added strain of Champions League football.

In fact, their European adventures boosted confidence even more, especially the historic 9-1 success away to RC Lens.

“It feels like every week you ask me about a new test of our maturity,” smiled Fabregas in his press conference.

“We knew this season would be special for us, there is so much motivation, but we know our path. This is an important match, we are coming off good form, but it is only a test to see where we can go. Inter remain the strongest team in Italy, we’ll see our level later.”

Although Como are giant-killers, they have never managed to beat Inter, including in last season’s Coppa Italia semi-final.

“We came close three times, but when Inter raise the bar, they become too strong for everyone. We need to play our football, do our thing, without anxiety or pressure. After this match, we’ll see where we are.”

Trevoh Chalobah is close to a full recovery, but “it’s not worth the risk,” so he remains out with Moise Kean, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai.

“I never stop learning from the best. The victory over Lens can happen once, if we’re lucky, in our lives, but Inter are the reigning Champions of Italy, won the Coppa Italia, played two Champions League Finals. Who knows, tomorrow we might pull a surprise with the perfect performance.”

Como were criticised for not having any Italian players last season, so with the pressure of the Champions League lists too, have tried to correct that.

It is paying off, with Mattia Liberali and 17-year-old youth talent Riccardo Cassano receiving senior Italy call-ups for the Nations League.

“I am very happy for Liberali, but the Cassano news was surprising, it shows Roberto Mancini wants to really go forward with youth. We coaches must help young players, be close to them and not put too much pressure on. Faith in your players is fundamental in football.”

Como didn’t have a youth academy in Serie C, but they are building it and the first talent to emerge is Matteo Papaccioli, who scored his debut Champions League goal midweek.

“When I took over the team in Serie B, they told me there was an Under-16 kid doing really well. He is so dynamic, has a strong mentality and hunger, I like players like this,” explained Fabregas.

“He had a serious injury that slowed his progress, but this is why I urge players to be ready and take every opportunity to show what they can do. Against Lens, I had to rest Douvikas at 6-0 up and told Papa to go and take centre-stage.”

That 9-1 victory was also watched by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who was impressed with the remarkable performance.

“I know Mikel very well, the day Mirwan Suwarso asked me to take the Como job, I called him and said I don’t know if I’m ready. He gave me important advice, which was to take the opportunity, even if I had doubts,” revealed Fabregas.

“Arteta sets a great example for all of us for what he is building at Arsenal. The patience shown by the club, even when there were moments of tension and he was eighth in the table, that is what we need too. I see him as inspiration for what we want to do in football.”

Fabregas was asked if he feels that he has improved as a coach in the last couple of years.

“It depends. If I deal with results better, absolutely not, but I do feel I’ve grown in my ability to prepare for and read games. Plus I haven’t been booked for dissent yet!

“Playing every three days changed my life, it helped me see things with the right balance. After Frosinone, Roma and Feyenoord, some had doubts, but winning six games won’t change my opinion any more than those setbacks did.

“We want to become a great team, with humility and keeping our feet on the ground. Remember, we’ve had great performances against Inter, but they win with details, including talent like Lautaro Martinez, Hakan Calhanoglu and Marcus Thuram. I wouldn’t change what I did,” concluded Fabregas.

I don’t know, I see Inter winning big and simple …

#1302. Ecosystems depend on people: don’t abandon them

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

The abandonment of villages in Japan is changing ecosystems. Studies are finding that biodiversity has declined in places that people have left behind.Credit: Tomohiro Ohsumi/Bloomberg/Getty

The idea that humanity is separate from the rest of the planet is deep-rooted, but wrong. Indeed, for most of human history, this has not been the case1. Many landscapes seen by European colonists as ‘wilderness’ were in fact tended by Indigenous people. This includes North America’s wildflower-studded oak savannahs and Australia’s fire-maintained ecosystems. Worldwide, traditional agricultural practices — which have been used for millennia, in some cases2 — have created ecological niches that support insects, amphibians, birds and plants, many of which have evolved together with humans.

When humans disappear, biodiversity takes a surprising turn

When humans disappear, biodiversity takes a surprising turn

People have always cleared land to some extent. But the scale of this practice has been unprecedented since the beginning of industrialization in the mid-eighteenth century, and especially since the onset of industrial farming. Intensive land conversion is the biggest driver of biodiversity loss. It’s a key reason why countries agreed four years ago to protect 30% of land and water habitats by 2030 (also called the 30 × 30 target).

That goal, however, explicitly did not intend for protected areas to be human-free zones3. Now, as Nature reports in a News feature, evidence is emerging that biodiversity does not necessarily thrive in places that humans leave behind. In Japan, where entire villages are being abandoned because of rural depopulation, the decline in traditional rice-farming practices and woodland management is reducing habitat availability for many birds, insects and plants that thrive in flooded paddies, along field margins or in open-canopy forests.

This example and others show that protected areas need humans to be responsible for specific tasks. These jobs include water management, the provision of grazing animals and ecologically informed forestry, such as using prescribed burning to prevent catastrophic megafires similar to those the world is seeing increasingly. The Americas, Europe and Australia will need many thousands of fire-trained professionals in the coming decades.

Protecting nature means valuing biodiversity

Protecting nature means valuing biodiversity

Land-tending practices also include traditional foraging and planting, the building of clam gardens on the coast and cutting down trees and shrubs to thin woodlands and stimulate fresh growth. Such work must be informed by modern ecology and conservation biology — which increasingly incorporate lessons from ecological knowledge that comes from, in some cases, millennia of practical field experiments.

These practices also need to be funded. Traditional farming and land-management techniques are expensive compared with industrial agriculture, which requires less labour and has huge yields. If humanity wants to preserve these traditional relationships with the planet and the biodiversity they support, governments will have to subsidize this work directly.

This is already being done in a limited way, through grants to farmers and in agricultural-biodiversity schemes. However, nations should consider providing robust and comprehensive support. Programmes could be based on the US Civilian Conservation Corps — created during the Great Depression in the 1930s — although standards would need to be updated to improve diversity and equity, and activities would have to be supported by evidence.

Biodiversity conservation has an evidence problem — it’s time to fix it

Biodiversity conservation has an evidence problem — it’s time to fix it

At a time of mass unemployment in the private sector, the corps was a publicly funded job-creation scheme that employed three million young men. Working in teams, they planted trees, prepared terraced fields, built roads and trails, erected fire towers and otherwise tended to US natural resources between 1933 and 1942.

Today, artificial intelligence is raising concerns not only about its environmental impacts4, but also that it could cause another phase of high levels of unemployment. Governments looking to establish schemes that could buffer their workforces against job losses associated with technological changes should consider investing in people’s relationships with land, water and biodiversity. It would be a mutually beneficial outcome: for people and the ecosystems we inhabit.

#1301. Harry Kane proves there is only one Ballon d’Or winner

Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.

Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

“I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.

And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”

Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.

The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.

Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.

It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.

“Unsere nummer neun,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.

Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.

Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.

Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.

Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.

But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.

Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐 His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw

And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.

Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW

It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI

Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.

When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.

Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶 He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF

They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?

It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.

It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.

Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.

They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.

Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.

Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.

Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.

I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.

We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.

The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.

They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.

For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.

I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.

Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.

When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.

He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.

In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover.

Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.

Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.

A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.

It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.

Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.

The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.

Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.

Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.

Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.

Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half.

Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.

A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.

Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.

Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.

Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign.

A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z

Arsenal deep in Bayern territory after Rice’s cross towards Eze glanced off the head of a defender. Bayern are keeping a good defensive shape though, Arsenal finding it difficult to penetrate. Arteta is preparing another pair of changes.

Luis Diaz with a snap shot that brings a sharp save from David Raya. On the balance of chances and threat created, Bayern have earned their lead. But still plenty of football to play. Arsenal have not scored from a set-piece this season, but they have looked dangerous tonight. They need another couple.

Neuer has just smashed into Stanisic, sweeping up a long ball Timber was chasing.

With Tzolis out and Saka now likely to be joining him on the sidelines, at what point does Arteta turn to Dowman in the league and Champions League? Obviously there are so many physical and defensive demands that are very difficult for a 16-year-old to meet... but the talent is there.

Arsenal enjoying plenty of territory and possession now, but you’d say Bayern look more likely to score on the counter-attack. Arsenal content to keep the ball and set themselves for a late assault.

Lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.

Karl and Diaz are on for Bayern, replacing Gnarby and Saibari. If anything that shifts Bayern up a gear. Arteta has also made a double change: Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes, and Gyokeres on for Havertz.

Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1300. Serie A | Torino 1-1 Lecce: A point each in chaotic stalemate

Torino and Lecce both stalled their dismal recent form with a point apiece, in a game delayed by a wonky goal-line, then decided by two deflected efforts.

The Granata had a strong spell of form with three straight victories, followed by back-to-back defeats against Como and Frosinone. Niccolò Fortini, Ricardo Rodriguez, Rolando Mandragora and Franco Israel were still out injured, but Alessio Cacciamani returned.

Lecce lost five of the last six games, culminating in a damaging home defeat to relegation contenders Genoa. Joel Monteiro joined Medon Berisha, Santiago Pierotti and Ivan Ilic on the treatment table, but Kialonda Gaspar’s two-match ban expired, with Lassana Coulibaly and Willem Geubbels available again on the bench.

There was a bizarre situation where the kick-off was delayed by 16 minutes because officials realised with goal-line technology that the lines had been drawn incorrectly and were not completely straight, so that had to be adjusted by the pitch staff.

The first real opportunity saw Lecce threaten to score directly from the corner flag, forcing Lucas Perri to scramble it out from under the bar.

Amar Fatah failed to make the most of the counter-attack after robbing Ardian Ismajli, while Sandro Kulenovic also didn’t take full advantage of a Tiago Gabriel slip.

Giovanni Simeone blasted over from a promising position, though if he had scored it would’ve been disallowed for handball.

The deadlock had to be broken by a massive stroke of luck, because the Simeone angled drive was perhaps not even on target before taking a huge deflection off Kialonda Gaspar to loop up over a helpless Wladimiro Falcone.

Lecce equalised in similar fashion, as the Konan N’Dri effort from the edge of the area looped up off Daniel Braganca to enter the net.

It remained open, Che Adams setting up Zakaria Aboukhlal to sting Falcone’s gloves with a side-foot finish, but Torino were the ones left with the biggest regrets.

At the 88th minute, first an acrobatic Adams overhead kick bounced off the woodwork, then Simeone was denied by Falcone on the follow-up from close range.

#1299. Celtic's Europa League win over Besiktas a welcome boost ... but Mika Baur says belief has always been there

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:32 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 14:41 EDT, 6 November 2026

It's fair to say that the way in which Martin O’Neill got Celtic off the mark in the Europa League against Besiktas divided public opinion.

For many of those viewing a starting line-up including Jordan Lotomba, Seb Tounekti and James Forrest, the veteran lucked out.

The opposing take was that O’Neill executed a managerial masterclass. That the belated introductions of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan constituted a textbook rope-a-dope approach.

Whatever the truth of the matter, and only O’Neill truly knows what it is, you could not possibly argue with the outcome.

Second best in the contest for an hour, Celtic improved markedly in the final 30 minutes and refused to accept a share of the spoils when it seemed destined to be their lot.

How you finish a match is, indeed, just as important as how you start it. And it helps, of course, when those who belatedly enter the fray bring not only goals but pace, panache and a positive attitude.

Midfielder Mika Baur has been a standout performer in an up-and-down season for Celtic

‘That’s what you want from the subs — to make an impact from the bench,’ said midfielder Mika Baur.

‘It says a lot for Camilo to accept the situation of starting on the bench. But to come on and make such an impact, producing in the big moments to score those two goals to win us the game was huge.

‘Ossie [Osmand] as well, he came on with a goal and assist. He won the ball as well and was working hard. I’m really glad for them.’

In every respect, Celtic needed a night like that. O’Neill walked off the team coach before the game knowing a loss would see him become the first manager in the club’s history to oversee five straight European defeats.

With the wider picture of just three wins in ten matches, the scatter gun had been trained on everyone at the club in recent days – the hierarchy, the players, the manager and his coaching staff.

‘The win was important after some tough weeks,’ Baur reflected. ‘But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good. There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves.

‘We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift. It was important to get those three points and we deserved it.

‘Hopefully, we can go forward with the confidence from this game.’

Given the air of gloom which has hung over the club lately, the Turks’ opener, stemming from a ludicrous tackle by Lotomba, felt for all the world like an extension of so much which had gone before.

From the minute Osmand levelled with his first touch, however, the entire dynamic of the evening changed.

Celtic found something deep within themselves that just hadn’t been there up until that point. The positivity on the field was mirrored by the buoyant mood in the stands.

The introductions of Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran turned Thursday's clash on its head

‘The fans helped a lot. You could feel the energy,’ said Baur. ‘It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win — it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

‘It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.’

Technically impressive and tactically astute, Baur caught the eye on Thursday, just as he has done in most of his matches since moving to Glasgow from Paderborn for £4.5million in the summer.

Whatever criticisms can justifiably be made of the club’s recruitment across a number of years, the German has already justified the faith shown in him.

It’s easy to forget that he’s still only 22. The level of scrutiny he’s being subjected to in Glasgow is a new thing. So far, however, he’s shown up well.

‘Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t,’ he shrugged. ‘But I hope people understand that as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

‘I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster. Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans — you feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost, but I am getting used to it.’

Having earned his first full cap in September after being called up by new Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, Baur has dropped back down to the Under-21s in the coming fortnight but takes only positives from his experience of the last international camp.

‘I can understand,’ he said. ‘There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

‘We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

‘I’m still with the Under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good.

‘European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see. I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time.’

#1298. Man City Fans Officially Give Up on ‘Useless’ Enzo Fernandez After Forest Loss

Manchester City suffered a shock 3-1 win away to Nottingham Forest and one of their star players has been called out for a disappointing performance at the City Ground.

Forest raced into a two-nil lead within twenty minutes when Jair Cunha struck in the sixth minute and Liam Delap produced a moment of magic for the second in the 18th minute. Enzo Maresca's men looked shell shocked as the two sides headed in for half-time.

A different City emerged for the second half and Rayan Cherki got them back into the game in the 52nd minute with a thumping effort. The visitors pushed for a vital equaliser, but it wouldn't come and their former academy product Delap bagged a brace with an almighty finish in the 73rd minute.

Whether games like tonight matter for City in the long run remains to be seen, with the likelihood being that they are relegated after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules. The club have maintained their innocence and their spending in the summer suggested all was well at the Etihad.

Their most expensive arrival, Enzo Fernandez, came with huge expectations after becoming somewhat of a talisman at Chelsea. A joint-Premier League record transfer fee of £125 million allowed the Argentine midfielder to reunite with Enzo Maresca.

Fernandez had made a strong start to life at the Etihad but has come off the boil in recent weeks. His display tonight has concerned his club's fans as he looked lost at times including in the second half when Murillo easily picked the ball off him and only the crossbar spared his blushes.

The 25-year-old should be a leader in this City team but he went missing, hooked in the 77th minute for Phil Foden. Not only did he struggle against Forest's impressive midfield, but he lacked creativity going forward.

As is always the case when a player moves for an astronomical fee, they are judged by each and every performance. One slip up immediately puts you under the microscope and that's the case for Fernandez tonight.

Fans on X have vented their frustrations with the Argentine and one supporter is unsure he's a good fit in the City midfield: "Enzo Fernandez isn’t creative enough to be a 10, not physical enough to be a DM, not smart enough to dictate play. He’s one of the most useless profile in football."

Another feels Fernandez has lost his touch since leaving Stamford Bridge: "Enzo fell off so badly."

One added: "Enzo Fernandez has cost a total of £1/4 Billion. Million miles off it. Not good enough. Not better than Oreily or Bouaddi in CDM."

Another went as far as to suggest Maresca could be made to pay for the Argentine's struggles: "This Enzo transfer is gonna be the end of Maresca. Our midfield is non-existent yet again and he can’t drop him because the money he forced the club the spend. I am done with him."

One added: "But honestly what does Enzo Fernandez do?"

Benjamin Mendy left Manchester City in 2023, with his career moving in a different direction since his exit.

Fernandez will have the international break to recharge and try and get back to his best ahead of the winter period. His side's defeat to Forest means they now trail league leaders Arsenal by six points and have lost three on the bounce.

#1297. Thomas Tuchel admits his relationship with Jude Bellingham is 'up and down' - but on the mend - as he reveals he's apologised to Kobbie Mainoo who is struggling at 'off a cliff' Man United

Published: 14:00 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 15:27 EDT, 6 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel says his rocky relationship with Jude Bellingham is on the mend after revealing he called his brother Jobe in to the England squad after some cajoling from the Real Madrid star.

Tuchel and Bellingham Snr have not always seen eye to eye during the German's time as England boss.

But Tuchel said today he hopes those days are behind him after he called 21-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe into this squad for next week's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place,' said Tuchel.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step.

Thomas Tuchel has admitted he has an up and down relationship with Jude Bellingham

'I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

With injury to Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for Thursday's Croatia game at Wembley, Tuchel sprung a surprise by elevating Jobe Bellingham from the Under 21s to the senior squad.

'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England,' explained Tuchel.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

Now Tuchel says he 'loves' to be Bellingham's coach after his brilliant World Cup campaign

Jude had a hand in brother Jobe being called up to the England squad for the first time

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

Tuchel's squad for what he insists are two important games was once again full of messages and insights into this thinking.

There was no room for Cole Palmer and Kobbie Mainoo after both players withdrew from the October campo with injuries. There was also no call up once again for Manchester City's Phil Foden.

Asked about Palmer, fit and ready now and in decent form at Chelsea, Tuchel said: 'It's not personal and we will never assume that he is not desperate to come and play.

'But the competition is on. It's about the ones who walk the walk and come to camp.

'Someone more intelligent once said to me: 'You cannot not communicate. You cannot not send a message.'

'So yeah. A nomination is always a message, yes.'

Tuchel revealed that he almost picked Foden – who hasn't played for England since March – after an upturn in his form but had second thoughts when he saw him relegated back to the bench at the Etihad Stadium.

'He is close and he will always be close,' said Tuchel.

'There were glimpses of the Phil Foden that we would love to see. He had these two matches with four or five goal involvements and assists and being so clinical.

Cole Palmer continues to be left out by Tuchel - while Phil Foden was close to a recall

'I got excited and thought: "That's it, that's, he found his mojo, he is getting back there". Then he dropped again and played again from the bench.

'I'm in love with him as a player. What is not to love?

'If you see the boy train it's just the highest, highest quality.

'But we're talking about numbers in an England shirt which are not in proportion to his talent and to his potential.

'If we can align this and become a regular City starter and be decisive, I think he has to be always an option.

'It was very close and it's also close for Eberechi Eze to keep his place with us. He's not starting for Arsenal.

'But the advantage was maybe that Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze come again into camp. The advantage was that they have been in camp last time.'

Thomas Tuchel has told how he apologised in front of the whole England squad to Kobbie Mainoo for not giving him a single minute during the summer's World Cup in America.

Mainoo cut a lost and frustrated figure during England's campaign after a succession of players were picked ahead of him in his central midfield position.

The Manchester United star has not made Tuchel's squad for the forthcoming Nations League games with Croatia and Spain after withdrawing from the last camp with injury.

Tuchel revealed: 'He was hugely disappointed from the World Cup, and deservedly so.

'I said it in front of the team, in front of the staff.

'I said: "Sorry that I didn't pick you, you did nothing wrong, that is on me".

'He was disappointed and I think it cost him a bit of confidence.

Tuchel has noted how Man United 'fell off a cliff' - causing issues for Kobbie Mainoo

'He was excellent in training and in the way he presented himself through the tournament.

'So he was never a problem, the way he carried himself.

'Then he pulled out of last camp. I was desperate to give him the minutes. Desperate to include him in this new start, in the Nations League.

'But he then missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

'He was injured then Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he suffers from that.'

#1296. Video: Lazio fans embrace team with love before big Napoli match

Lazio fans are banned from attending tomorrow’s match with Napoli, so they gathered in their thousands at the station to see Gennaro Gattuso and his players off.

It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Sunday at 11.30 GMT (12.30 CET).

There won’t be Biancocelesti supporters in the arena, as a history of violence between the sets of fans has made this a high-risk fixture, so the local authorities banned the sale of tickets to anyone in the Eternal City.

With that in mind, and considering also that ultras have been boycotting the home matches for over a year in protest at President Claudio Lotito, they put on a show of love for the team that is currently on top of the Serie A table.

Thousands of fans gathered at the Stazione Termini in Rome to see off the squad as they travel by train towards Naples.

They waved banners, flags and set off fireworks to celebrate the players and coach Gattuso for the club’s best ever start to a Serie A season.

Some players struggled to even make their way through the crowd without getting crushed by the affection of the supporters.

#1295. Man Utd 'Make Enquiry' to Sign Morgan Gibbs-White as Fernandes Replacement

Manchester United have a decision to make on the future of captain Bruno Fernandes in the coming weeks and months.

At the end of last season, it would have been a no-brainer for Man United to hand the Portugal international a new contract after a stunning season in which he recorded the most assists in a single Premier League season.

The 32-year-old has looked a completely different player this term though, and as well as being unable to replicate that form, he also made the disappointing decision to speak out publicly against manager Michael Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

Carrick dropped Fernandes to the substitutes' bench for the following game against Bournemouth in the league, which they lost 3-0, failing to bring him on even when they needed a goal.

Fernandes came back into the starting XI for the games against Chelsea and AS Roma, scoring a penalty at the second attempt against the Serie A outfit as the Red Devils came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 and send Old Trafford into raptures.

It was only the third game of the season that Fernandes had made an attacking contribution, with a goal and an assist, with his only other goals and assists coming in the club's other two victories against Ipswich Town and Sabah.

The facts from this season are that when Fernandes isn't on it, neither are United, and it has left club chiefs with a decision to make.

It seems likely they will exercise the option to extend his contract by 12 months whatever happens, in order to protect his value, but giving him a longer-term deal is more of a conundrum.

According to TEAMtalk, they are already considering potential replacements for their skipper, with Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White one player they are said to hold an interest in.

United are going to find it difficult to find someone who has been as influential as Fernandes has been for them when the time comes for him to leave the club, but Gibbs-White could be an interesting option.

TEAMtalk report that the Red Devils have already made enquiries as they assess the situation of the Forest star, and consider their long-term midfield and attacking options.

Unsurprisingly, the performances and attributes of the England international have caught their eye, especially after a stunning 2025-26 campaign for the Reds.

Gibbs-White's record (Premier League 2025-26)

Gibbs-White gives off Fernandes vibes in a number of ways, not least the fact that he is Forest captain and is highly influential to their attacking play.

Because he is six years Fernandes' junior, he also has the ability to cover more ground in the middle of the park more consistently, and his goal record is particularly impressive.

Based on last season, United would probably want more assists from Gibbs-White if he was to genuinely become the Portugal international's replacement at Old Trafford, but that could come.

The issue the Red Devils may have is how they prise the 26-year-old away from the City Ground, given the player was on the verge of joining Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2025, before Evangelos Marinakis personally intervened and convinced his captain to stay with a bumper £150,000-a-week contract.

Spurs are also still interested in Gibbs-White, ahead of a potential 2027 battle for his services.

What is clear is that whoever lands him in the future, they will be getting a player who looks ready to make a big impact at the biggest Premier League clubs.

Manchester United are keeping a close eye on Bournemouth ace Marcus Tavernier as Arsenal and Newcastle also monitor the winger

Eighteen years ago, Bournemouth were minutes away from being liquidated and playing in the fourth tier. On Thursday night, Bournemouth not only welcomed AC Milan in Europe; they did so as favourites, and then pummelled them.

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

#1292. Worse Than Porro: De Zerbi Must Drop Kudus After Leeds 1-0 Tottenham

Tottenham Hotspur may have felt that Jayden Bogle should have been sent off in their 1-0 defeat to Leeds at Elland Road on Saturday lunchtime, but it shouldn't deflect from what was a poor display from the in-form visitors.

Tottenham came into the clash in Yorkshire on the back of three successive Premier League victories, but in what was a pretty poor top flight game, they still looked second best compared to Daniel Farke's men for the majority of the game.

Spurs should have been full of confidence in the match before the two-week international break, but instead it was Noah Okafor's late winner that separated the sides.

The north London outfit will argue that they should have been playing against 10 men for the majority of the game after Bogle's first-half challenge on Mathys Tel, which went unpunished despite a four-minute VAR review.

That was a decision that former Premier League referee Mike Dean disagreed with on Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday, as he said it should '100%' have been a red card, especially after Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for something very similar last weekend.

A number of Spurs players simply didn't turn up at Elland Road, including Pedro Porro and Omar Marmoush.

The former struggled to deal with Gabriel Gudmundsson from a defensive point of view throughout the game, while he offered little threat in attack either.

The Spaniard was also fortunate not to see red following a challenge on Lukas Nmecha, having been harshly booked for an earlier tackle that led to De Zerbi being booked.

Meanwhile, Marmoush largely continues to flatter to deceive in a Spurs shirt following his summer move from Manchester City, and he offered little in the centre-forward position and on the left, where he moved after Tel had to be substituted.

Those two weren't the only poor performers on the day though, with Mohammed Kudus another to struggle badly.

While Porro and Marmoush were notably below-par in Yorkshire, Kudus produced one of his worst performances in a Tottenham shirt against Leeds.

The Ghana international started on the right wing against Farke's side, but he offered very little and was unable to provide the outlet they needed in the second half.

The 26-year-old was eventually replaced by Luca Williams-Barnett in the 83rd minute, and was handed a 3/10 rating by the Standard for his display.

Kudus is known for his ability on the ball but his dribbling was worse than normal, while he could only provide one accurate cross from seven attempts as Tottenham pushed for a goal.

To only win three out of the 13 duels he faced sums up the bad day at the office he had, and based on this display he will be fortunate to keep his spot in the XI against Ipswich after the international break.

While De Zerbi has made no secret of the fact that he is a big fan of Kudus having tried to sign him for Brighton previously, he can't continue to start matches if he performs like that.

The Italian boss has other options to pick from too with Luca Williams-Barnett, James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski all on the bench on Saturday, while Savio could be back in action after the international break after injury.

Tel could well be missing for some weeks after leaving Elland Road on crutches, but it doesn't mean that Kudus will start again against the Tractor Boys.

Based on this display, he should be dropped regardless.

Tottenham have some strong youngsters coming through.

#1290. Portugal boss Jorge Jesus claims Cristiano Ronaldo did NOT tell him he was retiring from international duty after fallout with superstar: 'I found out the same time as you'

Published: 16:01 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:09 EDT, 6 November 2026

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists he does not 'feel guilty' about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement and had no idea it was coming.

Ronaldo's explosive row with Jesus that escalated after he was left on the bench for a Nations League game and climaxed with the 41-year-old publishing a long statement hammering his manager, left their relationship in tatters.

And on Thursday, weeks after the dispute, Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal duty, bringing a sad end to his career on the international stage.

Jesus has now spoken for the first time about it, saying at a press conference: 'I don't feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision and, as such, his history cannot be ignored.

'I will never do that. Because he will always be a symbol, and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half. Sporting-wise, he has now made another decision, and I greatly respect his decision.'

When asked if he thought he was the reason for Ronaldo's retirement, the 72-year-old added: 'No... Maybe I rushed things, but not because of me. It was in his head that, with more or less call-ups, this was going to happen. It was always going to be during my tenure.

Jorge Jesus, pictured at a press conference on Friday, said he did not feel guilty about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement

'I didn't speak to Ronaldo because I was thinking about calling him up. From that moment on, I was going to have time to talk to him.'

And Jesus insisted he had no idea why Ronaldo chose now to quit, adding: 'You have to ask him... The absolute certainty I have is that Cris worked with me for a year. We were happy at the club where we were, we were champions. I respect his decision at this moment.

'He would always have been with me throughout all these years that we were going to work together. He was the one who would decide. I don't know why he made that decision. What I do know is that he knew his time was coming, he was the one who would choose. And he chose. Only he can answer that better than I can.'

Ronaldo scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

But he will not add to those achievements now – instead stepping away after 23 years playing for his country.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

His final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Ronaldo never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 23-year international career.

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures. But fans – and the man himself – will now have to embrace the next chapter as Portugal aim to move on without the most illustrious player in their history.

#1289. Liverpool 'Contact Agent' Over Surprise El Hadji Malick Diouf Transfer

Liverpool are eyeing a shock move for a Premier League star, according to reports, with FSG potentially realising the mistake they may have made.

Andoni Iraola's side could be in the market for a new left-sided defender in January with Milos Kerkez struggling for form since his £40million move from Bournemouth in 2025.

Kerkez shared responsibilities with Andy Robertson for the left-back role last season, and although the Scot has since moved on to sign for Tottenham, Kostas Tsimikas has returned from his loan at Roma and came in to start the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

While Kerkez is still Andoni Iraola's first-choice in that position, the Reds don't appear to be convinced about the Hungarian with alternatives eyed ahead of the January transfer window.

Pundit Alan Shearer certainly isn't, claiming that he believes Robertson is better than both Kerkez and Tsimikas.

Now, according to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch, Liverpool are plotting a potential move for El Hadji Malick Diouf at Brentford.

Diouf for Brentford in the Premier League

A fee of between £41.7million-£50m has been discussed, though the ex-Slavia Prague man has a contract to run until 2031 and Brentford might want more.

As well as Liverpool, Chelsea are said to be in the market for Diouf, according to the same report, with Xabi Alonso searching for a like-for-like replacement for Marc Cucurella, who left to join Real Madrid in June.

The 21-year-old joined Brentford in a £40m deal from West Ham in August, but has struggled for regular game time since. Indeed, Diouf has started just one Premier League match for the Bees and that came in the 2-2 draw at Aston Villa last month. The Senegalese was an unused substitute in the 2-0 win against Nottingham Forest last time out.

He was a standout performer for West Ham last season, despite the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League. It was no surprise to see him move back to the Premier League in the summer, with Brentford picking up his services despite interest from elsewhere.

But an exit from the Gtech Community Stadium has now been mooted, with Keith Andrews preferring Keane Lewis-Potter and even Aaron Hickey at left-back, meaning Diouf is third-choice.

Should Liverpool sign Diouf, he would add pace and an extra attacking threat down the left side. His athleticism is his biggest asset, and he is more than capable of getting up and down the flank.

Diouf has a high ceiling, and his former manager Nuno Espirito Santo heaped praise on him during his time at West Ham. “He’s a beautiful player," the Portuguese boss said in November 2025.

"He’s so sensitive, and the way he arrived here - I think he’s living a dream. He has a lot of talent, but he has things to improve. He’s like a diamond you have to polish. We have great responsibilities, but we have to enjoy what we do, and I think Malick does that.”

#1288. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.

We’ve lost our way if I’m totally honest but we’ll get back what it takes.

Carrick has come in, trailed by the Amazon cameras, sat down and made an address for five minutes before taking any questions. He acknowledges it’s not been good enough or what the club expects and that it’s got to get better. He’s talking about rebuilding this club based on humility, values and hard work and won’t let that go and that it inspires him going forward. “Yeah we’re in a moment where it’s not going well but we need to show exactly what it means and respect what it means to be here and what it takes to win,” he said. “You’re not entitled to win. It takes hard work.”

I think it’s important... recently we haven’t had a good time I think that’s obvious, I totally accept that.

We had five months of relative success and I was happy with many things I was seeing.

We haven’t done well enough recently. Wednesday was a bad night for a lot of reasons, it really hurt a lot, it hurt me to see how the game panned out.

As I said after the game, it was unacceptable.

Hopefully he will be in position by half-past, but it is not unlike managers to keep everyone waiting.

My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage.

Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my “strong personality”. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties’ needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.

Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact.

For all his brilliance and ruthlessness as a businessman, Sir Jim Ratcliffe has yet to convince that he has any feel for football. Just look at the performance of Ineos’s other prize assets this season: Lausanne-Sport lie 12th in the 12-team Swiss top flight after one win in 10, and Nice are a distant 13th in Ligue 1, having burnt through eight different managers during the petrochemical giant’s seven years in charge.

As James Ducker and Sam Dean explore in this piece, a succession of Manchester United managers have admonished their team for a lack of industry and athleticism. A number of factors may be to blame: recruitment errors, paralysing pressure and a bad dressing-room culture among them. It is time to get back to basics.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.
